title: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program
discipline: STEM, finance, semiconductors, semiconductor-related fields and information technology
deadline_central_display: No single date - each participating university sets its own application window per intake
deadline_note: Two intakes a year (Spring and Fall); each participating university publishes its own application window and nomination deadline. Some universities have already run their Spring 2027 programme information sessions in April 2026.
application_cycle: Two intakes a year (Spring and Fall), with each participating university setting its own application dates
status_note: The programme runs continuously, with the programme office opening calls for applications for Spring and Fall intakes. The Ministry of Education page for the programme was published on 23 December 2025 and remains current.
tuition_coverage_note: The Ministry of Education states that the Taiwanese government covers tuition fees and other administrative costs for up to two years.
benefits: Tuition fees and other administrative costs covered by the Taiwanese government for up to two years
Living allowance from the partner company of at least NTD10,000 per month
Internship allowance above or equal to the minimum wage
Priority employment opportunities with partner companies after graduation
eligibility: International students who have completed their second or third year at an overseas university
Junior college graduates and bachelor's degree holders
Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan
requirements: Meet the programme-specific academic and language requirements
Pass reviews of grades and performance by the school and the partner company to continue receiving funding in the second year
Fulfil the obligation to stay in Taiwan to work after graduation, based on the number of years of funding received
coverage: Tuition fees and other administrative costs for up to two years
Living allowance of at least NTD10,000 per month from the partner company
Internship allowance above or equal to the minimum wage
application_method: Apply online through a participating university's own application portal
A student nomination step may take place for opportunities such as the study trip
application_route: Apply online through a participating university's own application portal for the student nomination step, then submit self-study documents and research plan, attend interviews in both Chinese and English, and take part in the job matching interview with partner companies.
duration: A two-year degree programme plus internship, followed by a period of employment in Taiwan
description: INTENSE is a Taiwanese Ministry of Education programme that attracts talent to study and work in Taiwan through industry-academia cooperation. The government and industry jointly allocate resources to cultivate talent, emphasising the needs of domestic and international enterprises, while partner companies provide each student with a living allowance and internship allowance.

verification.notes: The programme's purpose, characteristics, eligible candidates, funding structure and work-in-Taiwan obligation were read directly from the Ministry of Education Taiwan English page for INTENSE (published 23 December 2025). The programme is hosted by the INTENSE Programme Office at National Taiwan University (intensepo2023.ntu.edu.tw), which publishes the tuition-fee cap of NT$50,000 per semester and NT$100,000 per year, the TOCFL and CEFR language requirements, the one-way airline ticket and necessary administrative fee, and the fact that the subsidy comes in two annual instalments based on actual enrolment and credit completion. Those details are programme-office specifications rather than MOE page statements and are therefore listed in the applicant_utility rather than treated as MOE-published terms. Note also that some archived 2024 pages on the programme office site carry 2024 dates that are no longer current.

applicant_utility: INTENSE is a career pathway disguised as a scholarship, so decide first whether you want it: students who accept the funding are obliged to stay in Taiwan and work for the partner company for a number of years equal to the funding they received. The government pays your tuition fees and administrative costs for up to two years, the partner company pays you at least NT$10,000 a month, and you get paid internships at or above minimum wage, with priority employment from the company when you finish. The focus fields are semiconductors, information technology, finance and related manufacturing, so if your degree is outside those areas this is probably not for you. Admission routes vary by university, so check the individual programme's language requirements - English-taught programmes generally ask for CEFR B1 while Chinese-taught programmes ask for TOCFL A2 in listening and reading, rising to B1 by the second year. At National Taiwan University the tuition-fee subsidy is capped at NT$50,000 per semester and NT$100,000 per year, paid in two annual instalments based on actual enrolment and credit completion, with a one-way air ticket and initial administrative fees included. Critically, the second year of funding is contingent on passing reviews of grades and performance by both the school and the partner company, so this is not an automatic two-year award.

title: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
deadline_central_display: April 23 to May 15 (the 2026 window has closed)
deadline_note: The published application period for 2026 was 23 April to 15 May 2026, applied for through the International Degree Current Student System. The renewal application takes place between April and May each year.
application_cycle: Annual renewal application between April and May, through the International Degree Current Student System
status_note: The 2026 application window closed on 15 May 2026; the next window opens in April 2027.
tuition_coverage_note: NTU states 'Tuition waiver up to NTD 100,000' and that this is exclusive of administrative fees, thesis advisor's fees, insurance, accommodation, internet service, credit fees and other such fees, borne by recipients.
benefits: Monthly living stipend provided by the advisor or the department, which may come with corresponding responsibilities
Master's students can receive the award up to their second year and doctoral students up to their fourth year
eligibility: Current international graduate student at NTU
Master's students under the 2nd year of study
Ph.D. students under the 4th year of study
requirements: Submit past years' transcripts or the Advisor Evaluation Form
Submit a Recommendation Letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship
The scholarship does not apply if the student graduates, takes a leave of absence or withdraws from NTU during the scholarship period
coverage: Monthly stipend of NT$8,000 for all colleges for master's students; NT$10,000 for the College of Liberal Arts, Law, Social Science or Management and NT$15,000 for other colleges for PhD students
application_method: Apply through the International Degree Current Student System during the published April-May window
application_route: Apply through the International Degree Current Student System, and note that the professor of the department the applicant belongs to makes the decision on NTU scholarships.
study_mode: Master's up to the 2nd year, doctoral up to the 4th year
duration: Master's students up to the 2nd year; doctoral students up to the 4th year
description: The National Taiwan University International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship provides a tuition waiver of up to NTD 100,000 and a monthly living stipend to current international graduate students at NTU, applied for through the International Degree Current Student System.

not_confirmed: deadline_date (the 2027 window has not yet been published)
verification.notes: Eligibility, award values by degree level, stipend tiers by college, note on fees borne by recipients, duration, renewal timing and required documents were read directly from NTU's Office of International Affairs scholarships page, published 23 April 2026. The record title in the catalogue, 'University of Awards NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship', appears to reproduce the source page's own heading. Note that the stipend is described as provided by the advisor or the department and may come with corresponding responsibilities, so the cash amount can vary. The NT$100,000 tuition waiver is exclusive of administrative fees, thesis advisor's fees, insurance, accommodation, internet service and credit fees, all of which recipients bear themselves.

applicant_utility: This one is worth chasing, but the structure matters more than the headline. The tuition waiver is capped at NTD 100,000 and explicitly excludes administrative fees, thesis advisor's fees, insurance, accommodation, internet service and credit fees, so do not assume your total bill disappears. The monthly stipend depends on both your college and your degree level: master's students get NT$8,000 across all colleges, while PhD students get NT$10,000 in the College of Liberal Arts, Law, Social Science or Management and NT$15,000 in every other college. Because the stipend comes from your advisor or department and may carry corresponding duties such as teaching or research work, this is effectively a private arrangement as well as a scholarship - check expectations with your prospective supervisor before you rely on the money. Applications run through the International Degree Current Student System between April and May each year, so time it with your department's own deadlines. Note the eligibility ceiling: the award stops at your second year as a master's student and your fourth year as a doctoral student, so it does not extend to the end of a longer programme.
